problems.title: A short proof of planar Jung’s bound
problems.statement_md: Let a compact planar set have diameter $w>0$ and smallest enclosing radius $R$. Prove $R\leq w/\sqrt3$. You may use the elementary optimality fact that the enclosing-circle center lies in the convex hull of its contact points, and planar Carathéodory’s theorem.
problems.hint_md: Write the center as a convex combination of at most three contact points. Expand the weighted sum of squared pairwise distances.

problems.title: The sharp inradius interval
problems.statement_md: Show that a planar width-$w$ body satisfies $w(1-1/\sqrt3)\leq r\leq w/2$. Identify equality cases.
problems.hint_md: Combine $r+R=w$ with Jung’s bound for one endpoint. For the other, compare the width of an inscribed disk with the width of the body.

problems.title: Cheeger scaling and domain monotonicity
problems.statement_md: For a bounded planar domain $\Omega$, let $h_C(\Omega)=\inf_{E\subset\Omega,\,|E|>0}P(E)/|E|$, with finite-perimeter measurable competitors. Show $h_C(a\Omega)=h_C(\Omega)/a$ for $a>0$ and $\Omega\subset\Lambda\Rightarrow h_C(\Omega)\geq h_C(\Lambda)$. Compute $h_C(B_R)$ in the plane.
problems.hint_md: Scale a competitor as well as the containing domain. For a disk, the isoperimetric inequality bounds every competitor’s perimeter-to-area ratio.

problems.title: The unique inner-radius equation for the Cheeger constant
problems.statement_md: For a planar convex body $K$ with inradius $r>0$, write $K_{-t}=\{x:x+tB\subset K\}$ and interpret $h_C(K)$ on its interior. You may use the theorem $h_C(K)=1/t_K$ where $A(K_{-t_K})=\pi t_K^2$. Prove that this equation has exactly one solution in $(0,r)$, and show how ordering all inner parallel areas orders the Cheeger constants.
problems.hint_md: Subtract $\pi t^2$ from the eroded area. Check continuity, strict monotonicity, and the endpoint signs before comparing roots.

figures.caption_md: Erosion retains the three disk centers and reduces every disk radius from one to 1−t.
figures.alt: Four nested rounded triangles illustrating increasing erosion distances.

problems.title: Cheeger extremizers at fixed constant width
problems.statement_md: You may use the theorem that $A(K_{-t})\geq A(T_{-t})$ for every width-$w$ planar body and $0\leq t\leq r(T)$, where $T$ is the Reuleaux triangle. Prove $4/w\leq h_C(K)\leq h_C(T)$, and identify an attaining body for each bound.
problems.hint_md: Use the eroded-area comparison for the upper bound. For the lower bound, combine isoperimetry for each competitor with the maximal area at fixed width.

problems.title: Radial integrals through intersections with disks
problems.statement_md: Let $K\subset B_R(0)$ be measurable and $g:[0,R]\to\mathbb R$ absolutely continuous. Prove $\int_K g(|x|)\,dx=g(R)|K|-\int_0^R g'(t)|K\cap B_t(0)|\,dt$. Explain why comparing radial moments requires fixing a center.
problems.hint_md: Write $g(s)=g(R)-\int_s^R g\prime(t)\,dt$ and interchange the order of integration.

problems.title: Why the Reuleaux triangle cannot minimize every radial moment
problems.statement_md: Center a width-one Reuleaux triangle $T$ and the radius-$1/2$ disk $D$ at their symmetry centers. Prove that for all sufficiently large $p$, $\int_T|x|^p\,dx>\int_D|x|^p\,dx$. Thus triangle minimality fails for some increasing convex radial weights.
problems.hint_md: The triangle has positive area at radii larger than $1/2$. Compare an exponential lower bound from that region with an upper bound for the whole disk.

problems.title: Translates collide exactly like equal disks
problems.statement_md: Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ have width $w$. Show that translates $K+a$ and $K+b$ have intersecting interiors exactly when $|a-b|<w$. Show that they touch at a single point when $|a-b|=w$, and are disjoint when $|a-b|>w$.
problems.hint_md: The forbidden translation differences form $K-K=wB$. Identify its interior and use strict convexity at contact.

problems.title: At most three constant-width bodies can meet without overlap
problems.statement_md: Let planar convex bodies $K_1,\ldots,K_N$ have positive constant widths, which need not be equal. Suppose their interiors are pairwise disjoint and they all contain one point $p$. Prove $N\leq3$. If $N=3$, prove that every $K_i$ is a Reuleaux triangle with a vertex at $p$, and their tangent sectors at $p$ partition the full angle. You may use the $120^\circ$ corner bound and its equality case.
problems.hint_md: Count the angles of the tangent cones at the shared point. Smooth boundary points occupy a half-plane.

problems.title: Three unit-width bodies in the unit disk
problems.statement_md: Determine the maximum number of planar convex bodies of constant width one that can be placed inside $B(0,1)$ with pairwise disjoint interiors. Boundary contacts are allowed, and the bodies need not initially be congruent. Prove that the maximum is three and characterize every maximizing arrangement. As a corollary, determine the maximum total occupied area. What changes if the closed bodies must be pairwise disjoint?
problems.hint_md: First prove that every body contains the disk center. The $120^\circ$ bound then counts how many bodies can meet there.

problems.title: For a prescribed shape the answer is two or three
problems.statement_md: Fix a planar body $K$ of width $w$. Show that two translates of $K$ always fit with disjoint interiors in $B(0,w)$. Prove that three congruent copies fit there if and only if $K$ is a Reuleaux triangle. Give an alternative proof for translates by showing that feasible translation vectors lie in $-K$ and must be pairwise at distance at least $w$.
problems.hint_md: For the two-copy construction, place each endpoint of a diameter at the origin in turn. For translations, combine the covering-center locus with the collision criterion.

problems.title: An explicit gap before four bodies can fit
problems.statement_md:
Let $R_4$ be the infimum of radii of disks that contain four planar unit-width convex bodies with pairwise disjoint interiors. The four shapes may be different. Prove the explicit bounds
$$(1+\sqrt2)(1-1/\sqrt3)\leq R_4\leq\frac{1+\sqrt2}{2}.$$
These are bounds, not a claim of an exact value. You may use the sharp inradius bound $r(K)\geq1-1/\sqrt3$.
problems.hint_md: Put an equal small disk inside each body. Among four nonzero center directions, two differ by at most $90^\circ$.

problems.title: The best lattice packing of a constant-width body
problems.statement_md:
Fix a planar width-$w$ convex body $K$. A lattice packing consists of the translates $K+v$ for $v$ in a rank-two lattice $\Lambda$, with pairwise disjoint interiors. Prove that the maximal density among such lattice packings is
$$\delta_{\rm lattice}(K)=\frac{2A(K)}{\sqrt3w^2}.$$
Compute this density for the disk and the Reuleaux triangle. Among width-$w$ bodies, which gives the largest lattice-packing density? Only lattice translates are considered here.
problems.hint_md: The shortest nonzero lattice vector must have length at least $w$. Reduce a lattice basis by subtracting integer multiples of its shortest vector.

problems.title: Diameter one alone gives no finite packing bound
problems.statement_md: Show that the unit-radius disk can contain arbitrarily many full-dimensional convex bodies of diameter exactly one with pairwise disjoint interiors. Explain why this does not contradict the three-body result for constant width one.
problems.hint_md: Use thin isosceles triangles whose equal sides run from the center to the unit circle.
